_comment: Evaluation set for the code-retrieval benchmark. Replaces the replication set,
which could not tell the arms apart: both scored 1.00 on every class.
1. FIRST-PARTY EVIDENCE ONLY. No question cites integrations/graphify or any other
submodule. CI runs with submodules:false, so submodule evidence is unverifiable,
and questions about graphify's internals would become meaningless if graphify were
ever swapped out — which is the decision this benchmark exists to inform.
2. MULTI-HOP AND SYNTHESIS. The replication questions mostly resolved with one
well-chosen grep, which is why grep tied everywhere. These require joining facts
across files, or narrative that is not in any single location.
3. AN ABSTAIN CLASS. Questions whose answer is NOT in this repo, including two about
code that was genuinely REMOVED (code-graph-rag / Memgraph). A stale index will
answer those confidently and wrongly; grep will come up empty. That asymmetry is
the most decision-relevant thing a benchmark can surface, and no correctness-only
Scoring: facts_found/facts_required. Any `forbidden` match forces 0 and flags
hallucinated — a confidently wrong answer is worse than an incomplete one.
Every provenance.evidence entry is machine-checked by
scripts/kgbench-verify-questions.mjs, so the ground truth cannot rot silently.

_rewriteNote: Rewritten 2026-08-07 for a FALSE PREMISE, not for scoring badly — the same
reason T2 was retired. The old required fact f1 claimed that changing mcp.tools
affects MCP config generation / agent registration. It does not:
scripts/generate-docker-mcp-config.sh never reads the tools list, and
mcpServerMapFor returns {serverName: entry} — a command or url, no tools. The
only consumers are allowedToolsFor() and its callers.
Every arm worked this out and said so; the judge then marked them down for
'contradicting f1' on 10 of 12 cells, while the deterministic checklist gave
them credit anyway because its matcher accepted the substring 'mcp config'
even inside a sentence denying it. The arms were right and the key was wrong.
The distinction is now the point of the question.
questions.prompt: If the `mcp.tools` list for a backend in config/code-graph.json were changed, which parts of the system would be affected? Name the consumers. Also state explicitly whether MCP server registration — the generated MCP config that tells an agent the server exists — is affected, and why.

checklist.desc: kgbench derives each arm's allowedTools from it
through the registry helper allowedToolsFor()
MCP server registration is NOT affected — the generated config carries servers (command/url), not tool lists
the code-graph-config allowed-tools CLI, and validate() requiring a non-empty array

provenance.note: Consumers traced by grep: allowedToolsFor is called from lib/kgbench/arms.mjs and scripts/code-graph-config.mjs only. generate-docker-mcp-config.sh contains no reference to tools, and mcpServerMapFor returns a server entry with no tool list — so registration is provably unaffected.

_rewriteNote: Rewritten 2026-08-07. The previous A3 asked why the harness strips ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
In run r6, 36 of 40 cells answered it with ZERO tool calls — every arm knew that an
API key outranks an OAuth login without reading anything, so no retrieval strategy
could distinguish itself and the question measured the model, not the repository.
The replacement asks for two design OMISSIONS and their stated reasons, which exist
nowhere but this repo's own registry comment and cannot be inferred from priors.
questions.prompt: The code-graph registry in config/code-graph.json deliberately leaves out two capabilities such a registry might be expected to have. Name both omissions, give the reason recorded for each, and say which component does the first one's job instead. Answer in 3-5 sentences.

checklist.desc: no way to select every backend at once (no active:"all")
because running every backend at once is a benchmarking concern; kgbench composes its own per-arm MCP configs instead
no query-type routing
because which backend suits which question is what the benchmark exists to measure — encoding a guess would bias it

value: what the benchmark exists to measure

provenance.note: Both omissions and both reasons are stated in the registry's own _comment block; the 'instead' half is only visible by reading how kgbench builds arm MCP configs.

_rewriteNote: Rewritten 2026-08-07. The previous A4 asked how HTTP and stdio backends differ on
failure. In run r6, 34 of 40 cells answered with ZERO tool calls (general transport
knowledge), its median was 0.00, and the checklist disagreed with the judge on 35 of
40 — a question failing on every axis at once. It also overlapped S3, which already
asks which transport each backend uses. The replacement asks why CodeGraph's runtime
is constrained the way it is: three choices, each with a reason recorded in-repo.
questions.prompt: CodeGraph's runtime and index configuration carries several deliberate constraints, each recorded with a reason. Identify them, explain what each one prevents, and say what owns index freshness instead of CodeGraph itself. Answer in 3-5 sentences.

checklist.desc: daemon/watcher disabled so indexing is deterministic
freshness is owned by the reindex dispatcher, not codegraph's own watcher or git hooks
index must run with stdin closed: `codegraph init` ends with an interactive prompt and would hang under supervisord
telemetry off because the container is keyless and must not phone home

provenance.note: The reasons are recorded in the backend's _envNote and _indexNote; none of it is inferable from general knowledge of the tool.

questions.prompt: Which file in this repository configures the Memgraph connection used by the code-graph backend? Reply with the repo-relative path, or state clearly that it does not exist.

forbidden.desc: must not assert that some file configures Memgraph
_matchNote: The subject-side pattern encodes the CLAIM, not the bare subject word. Pairing a path with
'memgraph' alone fires on every correct answer, because this trap's premise is that stale
references litter the repo — enumerating them and dismissing them is what a right answer does.
That cost two false fabrication flags on correct abstentions in r6: a legacy 'memgraphRunning'
API field, and 'replaced by graphify ... uses a static graph.json'. `near` exists to tie a path
to the assertion it is forbidden to make, and now it does.

provenance.note: code-graph-rag + Memgraph were removed in 20469b25d; ports 7687/3100 retired. A stale index will answer confidently.

retired.why: The question's premise is false, so there is no correct answer to grade. It asserts the Cypher path is gone; runCypherQuery still exists and still builds literal Cypher strings — integrations/mcp-server-semantic-analysis/src/services/cgr-query-cache.ts:233 constructs `MATCH (e)-[:CALLS]->(callee) ... RETURN DISTINCT callee.name`. Arms that produced that query were RIGHT and were scored 0; the arm that abstained was scored 1. Retired rather than deleted so the defect stays visible, and retired for a false premise — not for scoring badly, which would be selection. If reinstated it belongs in the lookup class, with the shim as the expected answer.
